_provenance: REAL — caselaw-graph POC. Source: CourtListener (Public Domain Mark) + SCDB issue areas, via idc9/law-net SCOTUS citation network (27,885 cases / 234,312 cites). Snapshot 2026-03-31. Method matches Fowler & Jeon (2008), 'The Authority of Supreme Court Precedent'.

carve_out_miranda.reading: Within the doctrinal neighbourhood, HITS authority cleanly recovers the self-incrimination / right-to-counsel landmarks — Miranda ranks #1.

top_authority: National Ass'n for the Advancement of Colored People v. Button (1963)
New York Times Co. v. Sullivan (1964)
National Ass'n for the Advancement of Colored People v. Alabama Ex Rel. Patterson (1958)
West Virginia State Board of Education v. Barnette (1943)
whole_scotus.reading: Naive global HITS authority is captured by a densely cross-citing First Amendment cluster (TKC), not the criminal-procedure landmarks — so its recall of our set is ~0. Raw in-degree does better (Miranda is #1 overall).

fowler_jeon_2008: Authority scores over the SCOTUS citation network yield rankings that 'conform closely to evaluations by legal experts'; Miranda is the highest-ranked modern case (also Gideon, Mapp, Brown). We recover this with PPR + carve-out HITS + in-degree.
tkc_caveat: Naive PageRank/HITS can over-reward densely cross-citing clusters (the TKC effect — seen here directly in the whole-SCOTUS authority list). Fowler's authority construction is the defensible global measure; we present this eval alongside it, not as the last word.
